authoredBefore: the first capture of the pilot

C1.name: window-selection-repeatable
C1.claim: Every run captures the intended VS Code window, chosen without human intervention.
C1.instrument: Normalized cross-correlation between the OBS source frame and a Playwright screenshot of the same window taken at the same moment, both reduced to 32x32 grayscale.

control.claim: The instrument can tell the intended window from a different one.

C1.ambiguityNote: Selecting a window by title alone passes in a sterile environment and captures the wrong window in a real one. The harness enumerates every candidate match and REFUSES to record when more than one matches, rather than silently taking the first.

C2.name: no-unrelated-desktop-pixels
C2.claim: A window overlapping the target contributes no pixels to the capture.
C2.instrument: A harness-launched occluder window filled with pure magenta (255,0,255) is raised over the target; the target frame is scanned for pixels within L-infinity distance 24 of magenta.

control.claim: The magenta detector fires when magenta is genuinely in frame.

C3.name: usable-resolution-under-display-scaling
C3.claim: The capture is at the window's physical pixel size, not a downscaled logical size.
C3.instrument: OBS frame dimensions compared with the target window's physical client-area rectangle (Win32 GetClientRect on the HWND, DPI-aware).
C3.note: The measured display scale is recorded per run. A pass at one scale is a claim about that scale only, and the outcome record must say which scale was exercised.

windowResizeVariant.claim: The capture tracks the window's actual pixel size rather than a fixed canvas.
windowResizeVariant.instrument: One additional run with the target window deliberately resized to a different physical size; frame dimensions must follow it within the same tolerance.

C3.scalingLimitation: This machine reports 100% display scaling (LOGPIXELSX 96, DESKTOPHORZRES == HORZRES == 1920). Changing the operator's live display scaling to exercise 125%/150% is an intrusive change to their working desktop and is NOT performed. The resize variant tests the same dimension-blindness failure mode without touching display settings, and the residual -- that no scaled display was exercised -- is recorded rather than papered over.

C4.name: step-events-align-with-captions
C4.claim: Caption cues retimed from the step-event stream land inside the recording.
C4.instrument: walkthrough_run finalize retimes captions from the step-event stream anchored at run-started; cue windows are compared with the recording duration OBS itself reports.

C5.name: dependency-absent-fails-clearly
C5.claim: Every way the dependency can be missing produces a named failure, and the walkthrough still completes without a video.
C5.instrument: Three induced variants, each run for real.

C6.name: deterministic-cleanup
C6.claim: Nothing the harness created outlives the run, including when the run fails part way.
C6.instrument: Post-run assertions after each of the ten runs and after one deliberately induced mid-run failure.
C6.restoreNote: The pilot enables obs-websocket's server (one boolean in the operator's config) because neither --websocket_port nor --websocket_password turns it on, and puts the file back byte-for-byte afterwards. It also clears and does not leave OBS's .sentinel run markers, whose leftovers raise a modal 'crash detected' dialog on the next launch -- which is how a harness silently hangs a later run.

C7.name: no-monitor-capture-ever
C7.claim: The pilot never captures the screen, only windows the harness itself launched.
C7.instrument: The set of OBS input kinds the harness creates is recorded per run and asserted; every captured window is matched to a harness-owned process id.
C7.amendment: AMENDED before the first capture (journaled). Probing the environment found the operator's DEFAULT OBS scene collection carries a live webcam (NexiGo N940P), a microphone and Desktop Audio. The harness already creates its own scene collection, but an unasserted safety property is a hope -- and this one is the operator's camera. Camera and audio input kinds are now forbidden explicitly, the harness's scene must contain exactly the one window-capture source it created, and the recording must carry no audio track. Captures taken before this amendment: zero.

honestFail: Any criterion unmet, or fewer than ten consecutive clean runs, is a FAIL. A fail ships no recorder; the measurements are the deliverable and manual-only degradation stays intact.
